change.summary: Propagate the existing bounded failover selection signal into credential-provider acquisition so a stalled provider cannot retain the serialized routing lock or a half-open probe after the request deadline; dispose any SecretLease that resolves after abandonment.

before_implementation.observed_failure: The first request received its bounded total-deadline response, but the stalled credential acquisition retained the routing lock so the second new request returned HTTP 503 instead of the expected HTTP 200.
before_implementation.bounded_cleanup: The synthetic provider gate was released during fixture cleanup and the command exited normally.

failure_injections: a synthetic credential acquisition remains pending beyond the 100 millisecond total failover deadline
the serialized routing lock and unconsumed half-open probe are released after cancellation
a subsequent new request retries the recovered synthetic provider and succeeds
the first SecretLease is disposed when its late acquisition resolves

covers: HTTP/SSE bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
WebSocket bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
durable and abortable automatic routing plus durable manual routing
abortable credential acquisition and late SecretLease disposal

deployment.reason: The previously proven sudo root-GID transition failure and non-writable /opt/codex-account-router boundary are unchanged.

remaining_limits: 0.2.15 is verified but is not active until a host-privileged operator runs the rollback-capable router-only deployment script.

AbortSignal abandonment does not cancel provider-internal work already in progress; a late SecretLease is disposed on resolution, but provider implementations remain responsible for bounding their own underlying operations.
The timed-out request is not replayed or resumed. Only a later new request can retry after provider recovery.
The tests use synthetic accounts only and do not qualify a real A-to-B switch.
Real two-account verification remains blocked until explicit enrollment authorization.
